It may be safely trusted as proportionate and of good issues, so it be faithfully imparted, but God will not have his work made manifest by cowards.
Some, perhaps, will think that Arnold was unappreciative and cold, but dispassionate readers will be inclined to agree with his judgment of our great American.
Let me live onward; you shall find that, though slower, the progress of my character will liquidate all these debts without injustice to higher claims.
Life lies behind us as the quarry from whence we get tiles and copestones for the masonry of to-day.
The true scholar grudges every opportunity of action passed by, as a loss of power.
As such it is precious as the sign of an indestructible instinct.

This perception of the worth of the vulgar is fruitful in discoveries.
Shakspeare employed them as colors to compose his picture.

There the boy Emerson found them and learned to love them, and the man Emerson loved them but the more.
I greet you on the recommencement of our literary year.
And let no one object that it is too general; that more practical, positive direction is what we want....

We worship it to-day because it is not of to-day.
Men have looked away from themselves and at things so long, that they have come to esteem the religious, learned, and civil institutions as guards of property, and they deprecate assaults on these, because they feel them to be assaults on property.

These signs, like paper money, may be counterfeited or stolen, but that which they represent, namely, knowledge and virtue, cannot be counterfeited or stolen.
He has read and seen but conceals the labor.
Thus far, our holiday has been simply a friendly sign of the survival of the love of letters amongst a people too busy to give to letters any more.
When we have new perception, we shall gladly disburden the memory of its hoarded treasures as old rubbish.

Marvell's wit and distinguished abilities rendered him formidable to the corrupt administration of Charles II., who attempted without success to buy his friendship.
There were four of importance: the Olympic, held every four years; the Pythian, held every third Olympic year; and the Nemean and Isthmian, held alternate years between the Olympic periods.
There are no fixtures to men, if we appeal to consciousness.
Must we not suppose somewhere in the universe a slight treachery and derision?

The thought is not then taken hold of by the right handle, does not show itself proportioned and in its true bearings, but bears extorted, hoarse, and half witness.
There is almost no kind of self-reliance, so it be sane and proportioned, which fashion does not occasionally adopt, and give it the freedom of its saloons.
I will receive from them, not what they have, but what they are.
Vice is the absence or departure of the same.
